newsitem.title: USA: Phar-Mor, Shopko to merge; Revco bids for Big B.
newsitem.headline: Phar-Mor, Shopko to merge; Revco bids for Big B.

text.p: Major U.S. drugstore chains Monday announced the latest in a series of industry consolidations, as Phar-Mor Inc. and ShopKo Inc. agreed to a mega-merger and Revco D.S. Inc. launched an unsolicited takeover bid for Big B Inc.

Phar-Mor and ShopKo will form a new holding company in a $1 billion deal, with combined annual sales of about $3.2 billion from 232 stores in 29 states. The partners will become operating subsidiaries of the new firm, Cabot Noble Inc.
Revco, the nation's second-largest drugstore chain, launched a cash tender offer worth $330 million for the remaining stock of Big B Inc. that it does not already own.
The proposed transactions came just one month after Thrift Drug Inc., a unit of J.C. Penney Co. Inc., said it was buying drugstore chain Fay's Inc. for $285 million.

Analysts said the deals herald a growing number of industry mergers and acquisitions, as dozens of second- and third-tier drugstore chains combat drug pricing pressures or cannot afford costly computer upgrades that are essential in today's world of managed health care.
"The economics of the industry favour size these days. That wasn't necessarily the case five years ago," said Joseph Ronning of Brown Brothers Harriman.
Phar-Mor and Shopko said their merger, which involves a three-way exchange of shares, will save the companies about $15 million to $20 million annually.

Based on current sales figures, the companies will have nearly $500 million of combined annual pharmacy sales, an additional $500 million of sales in drug store-related products, and about $1 billion in general merchandise sales.

Green Bay, Wis.-based ShopKo has 130 stores in 15 states, primarily in the Midwest, Pacific Northwest, and Mountain regions. Youngstown, Ohio-based Phar-Mor has 102 stores in 18 states, primarily in Ohio, Pennsylvania and Virginia.
About two-thirds of the two companies' sales is in similar merchandise categories, particularly in the area of pharmacy, health and beauty aids, and general merchandise.
The remaining $1 billion in combined new company sales includes revenues from ShopKo's ProVantage, Inc., health care subsidiary and other merchandise areas that the companies do not now share.

Under the share exchanges, each ShopKo common share will be exchanged for 2.4 shares of Cabot Noble stock, subject to adjustment. Each share of Phar-Mor common stock will be exchanged for one share of Cabot Noble stock.
ShopKo's stock fell 12.5 cents to $16.125 on the New York Stock Exchange. Phar-Mor slid 75 cents to $7.375 on Nasdaq.
After the share exchanges, Supervalu Inc., which owns 46 percent of ShopKo, will sell the Cabot Noble common stock it receives to Cabot Noble for about $248.4 million.
ShopKo public shareholders will end up owning about 77 percent of the combined company, compared with their current 54 percent ownership of ShopKo.

Revco, which owns 5.4 percent or 1.19 million of Big B's 22 million common shares outstanding, said it launched the $15 per share tender offer for Big B after the company rejected its friendly proposal.

The offer, which expires Oct. 7, represents a premium of 53 percent over the $9.81 average closing price of Bessemer, Ala.-based Big B's stock for the 90-calendar day period ended Friday. The stock soared $3.25 to $15.875 on Nasdaq.
Revco rose 12.5 cents to $25.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Twinsburg, Ohio-based Revco said it expected the deal would enhance its earnings per share in the first year after the merger.
Big B has 389 drug stores and nine Home Health Care stores in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi and Tennessee.
Revco operates 2,184 stores in 14 contiguous Midwestern, Southeastern and Eastern states. It has more than 32,000 employees.
